main_text.p: toto terrarum orbe, christiana Religio fuerit propagata, quod & idem Iustinus in Dialogo cum Tryphone his verbis demonstrat: [Atqui ne unum quidem est genus mortalium, siue barbarorum, siue Græcorum, siue etiam aliorum omnium quocunque appellentur no-mine, vel Amaxobiorum, vel Noma-dum domo carentium, vel in tentoriis viuentium: inter quos per nomen cru-cifixi Iesu, supplicationes & gratiarum actiones Patri fabricatori rerum om-nium non fiant.] Quid igitur hærent? cur non suas conscribunt copias? cur non in puluerem & aciem contra Imperatorem cateruatim descendunt? quòd si vnquam,pro aris quidem & fo-cis, pro religione & vita faciendum foret. Vis vt vno expediam verbo,quia Christiani,quorum quotidiana praxis est patientia,& professione teffera obe-dientia:imò tibi expediet Iustinus in A-pologia ad Antoninum:quia spes nostras non præsentibus rebus,fixas habemus,per-cussores nihil moramur : præsertim, cùm moriendum nobis esse sciamus. En Christianorum patientiam:Nos solum Deum

page.notes: The running head carries the book marker "LIB. II." at the right, which is left out as a number. The page number is printed in an old-style figure that reads as 80; the first digit is doubtful. The text continues beyond the bottom of this part. The sign before "Antoninum" (a curved stroke over the A) is doubtful and may be a printer's ornament or a reference mark; it is not transcribed. The word "adc-" is the catchword, a hyphenated start of the next line, not a complete word. Some italic letters at the line ends are faint, and the reading of "cùm" (accent) and "præ" (ligature) follows the scan as best as possible.
